title: Three Springs and One Short Seat
subtitle: 品格修养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 品格修养（人与自我·做人与做事·优秀品行与道德品质）
meta: 主题语境：品格修养（人与自我·做人与做事·优秀品行与道德品质）　|　核心词汇：honour　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 honour 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1976 the headmaster ① awarded the honour that no student in the hall would have described, and he said the awarding was the whole of the spring. The ② honour, meaning the respect itself and not the seat, ran three springs and stayed undescribed in the book; a honour, he said, is the only thing in a hall that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ honour in that hall had the same short seat beside it, and the ④ honour at the far platform, meaning the prize they kept for the children to win and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A honour, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the headmaster said the describing is the part that fills three springs.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the honour was the whole of the matter, meaning the trust and not the respect. The ⑥ honour, meaning the trust and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; honour, he said, is either something you award or the only word that means both a respect and a trust. He said the trust is the part they remember.

By 1981 the ⑦ honour had become a line in a certificate, and the certificate had become an argument about the short seat. The ⑧ honour of the whole thing, the headmaster wrote in October, was one hall and three springs of describing; honour, he said, is either the prize at the far platform or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ honour I remember is the respect described in the certificate, which closed in 1983 and is still described as the quietest in the hall. A ⑩ honour, my mother said in 1985, is the only respect that improves by being described; every honour, she said, is a trust that has agreed to look like a respect. She said the trust was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 荣誉；敬意（指礼堂里每一项旁边的那一项）
B. n. 荣誉；敬意（指那项敬意本身，与座椅相对）
C. 固定搭配：award the honour 授予这项荣誉
D. n. 荣誉；敬意（指留给孩子们争取的那一项）
E. n. 荣誉之事（抽象总称，指一处礼堂的荣誉之事）
F. n. 荣誉；敬意（指证书里写到、被记下的的那一项）
G. n. 信任、重托（指一件事里人人都看重却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 重托（抽象总称，指人人都看重却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: awarded the honour that no student in the hall would have described
The honour, meaning the respect itself and not the seat
the honour at the far platform
the honour was the whole of the matter
the honour had become a line in a certificate
The honour of the whole thing
A honour, my mother said in 1985

answers.why: award the honour 意为“授予这项荣誉”，1976 年那位校长把礼堂里没有一位学生肯描述的一份荣誉做了一遍。
honour 意为“荣誉；敬意”，指那项敬意本身而不是座椅，它经过了三个春天而在簿子上没有被描述。
honour 意为“荣誉；敬意”，指礼堂里每一项旁边的那一项，每一项旁边都有同一把小小的座椅。
honour 意为“荣誉；敬意”，指最远那方讲台留给孩子们争取的那一项，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
honour 意为“信任、重托”，指一件事里人人都看重却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份信任就是那件事的全部。
honour 意为“重托”，指人人都看重却无人提起的那样东西而不是那项敬意，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
honour 意为“荣誉；敬意”，指证书里写到、被记下的的那一项，到 1981 年这一项成了证书里的一行。
honour 意为“荣誉之事”，校长十月写道，整件事的荣誉之事是一处礼堂和三个春天的描述。
honour 意为“荣誉；敬意”，我记得的是证书里描述过的那一项，1983 年颁出了，至今仍被说成礼堂里最安静的一项。
honour 为抽象总称，母亲 1985 年说，荣誉是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的敬意。
